newsitem.title: USA: U.S. calls on Kabila to open corridor for refugees.
newsitem.headline: U.S. calls on Kabila to open corridor for refugees.

text.p: The United States called on Tuesday on Zaire rebel leader Laurent Kabila to open corridors so that hundreds of thousands of Rwandan refugees trapped by fighting can return to their homeland.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said more than 200,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees who have been in eastern Zaire since a civil war in Rwanda in 1994 had scattered from camps in the area because of fighting.
"We don't believe that any of the refugee camps in eastern Zaire are occupied," Burns told reporters.
"We're formally calling today for Mr Laurent Kabila to allow the opening of these corridors (from Zaire to Rwanda) so that innocent people can flee the fighting. It's a desperate situation," he said.

Tutsi-led rebels, who took up arms last October when authorities tried to expel them to their ancestral homeland in Rwanda, have seized a vast stretch of eastern Zaire with seemingly little resistance by Zaire's army.

Kabila says he is determined to end Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko's 31-year-old rule. He has spurned international pressure for a ceasefire, insisting on direct negotiations with the ailing Mobutu, who is in France.
Many but not all of the more than one million Rwandan refugees in Zaire managed to return home last December, and Burns said Washington wanted to see that repeated.
He said State Department refugee coordinator Phyllis Oakley discussed the situation on Tuesday by telephone with Emma Bonino, the European Union's humanitarian affairs commissioner.

He said they had agreed on a view, backed also by U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees Sadako Ogata, that the corridors should be opened, "and that all of us have an interest in contributing humanitarian assistance to these refugees."
The issue also figured prominently in talks in Washington on Tuesday between U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy, Burns said.
